Simulation Study: Resampling Choice and Null Rejection Rates

Source: R/resampling_study.R
run_resampling_fwer_study.Rd

Estimates the probability of at least one false positive under a global null for permutation-based methods, comparing:

  • default voxelwise sign-flip calibration, and

  • subject-level sign-flip calibration via null_fun.

Usage

run_resampling_fwer_study(
  n_sims = 50,
  dims = c(12, 12, 12),
  n_subj = 20,
  n_perm = 200,
  alpha = 0.05,
  cluster_thresh = 2.5,
  fwhm_vox = 2,
  tail = c("pos", "two"),
  two_sided_policy = c("BH_all", "split_q"),
  seed = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

n_sims

Number of independent null simulations.

dims

3D volume dimensions.

n_subj

Number of subject maps used to construct the group map.

n_perm

Number of permutations per method call.

alpha

Target level used for TFCE (alpha) and cluster-FDR (q).

cluster_thresh

Cluster-forming threshold for cluster_fdr().

fwhm_vox

Smoothness (voxel units) used when simulating subject maps. Scalar or length-3 vector.

tail

Tail for both methods: "pos" or "two".

two_sided_policy

Two-sided policy for cluster_fdr().

seed

RNG seed.

verbose

If TRUE, prints simulation progress.

Value

A list with components:

draws

Per-simulation results with columns sim, method, null_model, reject, time_sec.

summary

Aggregated rates and timing with columns method, null_model, n_sims, reject_rate, mc_se, ci_low, ci_high, mean_time_sec.

params

Study parameters used.

Details

Under the complete null, this "any discovery" rate coincides with the FDR metric for cluster_fdr() and is directly comparable to target level.

Subject maps are simulated as smoothed Gaussian fields and standardized per subject. A subject-level sign-flip null is created with make_null_fun_subject_signflip and injected into tfce_fwer / cluster_fdr using null_fun.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
st <- run_resampling_fwer_study(
  n_sims = 20,
  dims = c(10, 10, 10),
  n_subj = 12,
  n_perm = 50,
  alpha = 0.1,
  seed = 1
)
st$summary
} # }
